content.intro: You receive an email from your university inviting you to join a research study about music preferences.

questions.question: First, how often do you listen to music? Do you listen daily, weekly or less often?
What genres or types of music do you usually enjoy listening to? For example, do you prefer classical, rock or jazz music?
Can you tell me about a concert or live music event you would like to attend? Why would you make that particular choice?
Do you agree or disagree with this viewpoint? Why?
First, do you have any specific routines or practices you use to maintain your physical well-being? If so, what are they?
Can you describe any dietary choices or habits that you follow to stay healthy?
If you could make one significant change to your diet or exercise routine to stay healthy, what would it be? Why would you make that particular choice?
Do you agree or disagree with this viewpoint? Why?

content.intro: You have volunteered for a research study at your university about exercise programs.

questions.question: First, do you think exercising daily is important for good health? Why or why not?
What kind of exercise or fitness routine would you recommend? Why?
For that same friend or family member, what do you think might challenge them the most about a regular exercise program? How would you help them through this challenge?
What do you think would be a good reward for the program you created and why?

content.intro: You have volunteered for a research study at your university about childhood education.

questions.question: First, did you enjoy your school experience as a child?
What made that project or activity special? Do you feel like that technology prepared you for life after school? Why or why not?
Do you agree or disagree with this viewpoint? Why?

content.intro: You have signed up for a study run by a university research group that is investigating education experiences.

questions.question: First, which do you think is more important for a college? Offering a wide variety of courses or having small class sizes?
Would you prefer to study by yourself or with the group? What would make you choose one over the other?
What are your thoughts on this? Do you agree or disagree? Why?
Do you think online learning will someday completely replace in-person learning?

content.intro: You received an email from your university inviting you to join a research study about entertainment preferences.

questions.question: What kind of movies do your family or friends generally like to watch? For example, do they prefer action movies, comedies, dramas, or other types?
When you watch a movie, do you prefer to watch after work or school on weekdays? Or do you like to watch during the weekends? Why?
Do you think that movie theaters will continue to exist in the future? Why or why not?
Do you agree with this idea? Or do you think there are other, more effective ways to educate people?

questions.question: First, do you take any specific actions to reduce your environmental impact, such as recycling or conserving energy?

if you had the chance to participate in an ecological or nature-based activity, such as a community cleanup effort or tree planting event, what would you do and why?

What is your opinion and why?
Do you agree or disagree with this belief? Why or why not?

content.intro: You have agreed to participate in a research study about people's experiences with setting personal goals.

questions.question: What was it?
In general, how do you handle difficulties or obstacles that come up while working toward what you want to achieve?
In your opinion, how important is goal setting for personal growth?
Do you think children should be taught to set personal goals from an early age? Why or why not?

content.intro: You have volunteered for a research study about people's experiences with commuting.

questions.question: First, what kinds of places do you usually go to during the week and how do you get there?
Can you describe how someone in your family or a friend usually travels to work or school? How much time does it take and what transportation does the person use?
While others think location doesn't matter much, what do you think? why?
Which view do you agree with and why?

content.intro: You received an email from your university inviting you to join a research study about personal finance.

questions.question: First, how often do you review your money management, such as tracking your expenses or budgeting? Do you do this weekly, monthly or less often?
